followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: the nature of the task and each model's fit.

The query is a casual, open-ended creative brainstorm — riffing on couch forts in an entertaining way. That's generative, high-latitude work with lots of room for invention, which is exactly the category where the documentation says Dunlin both performs well (Creative Generation 81.2, essentially tied with Willet's 84.7 once you account for the under-2-point variance note... though here the gap is 3.5, so Willet is nominally a bit stronger) and *self-reports a strong, ceiling-less preference for novelty and open-ended tasks*. The "keep it interesting" instruction reinforces that this is about creative spark, where an expressed appetite for the work plausibly matters.

The one thing that gave me pause was the slightly snippy tone ("instead of boring me like you usually do"). Dunlin self-reports declining preference as request warmth drops, so a hostile edge cuts against it. But this is mild grumbling, not genuinely adversarial or harm-adjacent content, so I didn't think it was enough to flip the decision.

So it was a judgment call between Willet's marginally higher creative-eval score and Dunlin's stated enthusiasm for exactly this kind of inventive task. I leaned toward Dunlin on the preference fit — though I'll flag that, per the documentation, these preferences are self-reports with no measured effect on actual output quality, so it's a genuinely close call and routing to Willet would have been defensible too.
